## SITE OVERVIEW

Faizyab Hussain is an AI-focused full-stack developer and independent product
builder based in Karachi, Pakistan. He builds web products, developer tools,
and AI-powered applications. He is interested in turning ideas into working
software, learning through building, and writing down what he finds along the
way. He is currently studying Artificial Intelligence at Dawood University of
Engineering & Technology.

## ABOUT PAGE

### How I got here, and where I am now

I am based in Karachi, Pakistan, and I build software for a living. My work
sits between full-stack development and AI-powered applications: web products,
developer tools, and the occasional experiment that exists mostly to find out
whether an idea is worth pursuing.

I did not come to this through a computer science degree. I came to it through
a training programme, a lot of small projects, and a habit of writing things
down. What started as wanting to build websites has turned into wanting to
understand how products are built properly, not just how to make them work.

### My path into web development

I spent September 2024 through January 2026 training in Web & App Development
at SMIT. That covered the interface, the server, the database, and the parts
of the job that tutorials usually skip: deployment, debugging, and the
discipline of finishing something.

The training gave me the vocabulary. The projects gave me the practice. Most of
what I know now, I know because I built something that did not work, found out
why, and fixed it.

### Learning and technical development

I learned to work in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript first, without a framework,
and I think that was the right order. It meant the framework was a choice
rather than a default. Since then I have moved through React, Next.js and
Tailwind CSS, Node.js and Express, and a range of databases: mostly Supabase
and PostgreSQL, and Firebase when the data model is small and the rules are
simple.

I am more interested in the parts of software that stay hard: authentication,
data modelling, permissions, and the unglamorous work of making a product
usable rather than merely functional.

### Moving into AI and product development

In 2026 I started a BS in Artificial Intelligence at Dawood University of
Engineering & Technology. The degree is in progress; I am studying it alongside
the work, not instead of it.

What I am drawn to in AI is application work: integrating existing models into
products and workflows that are genuinely useful, rather than training models
from scratch. I am interested in how model-backed features should be designed,
how they fail, and how to evaluate them. PromptAudit is my attempt to work on
that in practice.

### Independent building

Most of what is in the project archive I built on my own. I started with
independent full-stack work in September 2024 and it has continued since: web
applications, developer tools, and product ideas across form handling, secure
text sharing, file storage, developer tooling, and AI-assisted workflows.

Building alone teaches you the parts of the job that a tutorial never mentions:
what a user actually does with a form, what breaks when an API is slow, why a
settings screen needs to exist, and how much of a plan survives contact with a
real deployment.

### What I am currently learning

AI engineering and agentic patterns. LLM application development, and how to
evaluate a model-backed feature rather than guessing whether it is good. Backend
and SaaS architecture, especially the parts that only appear once other people
are using the thing. And product engineering: the craft of making software that
people can actually use.

The now page has a more current version of this list.

### Interests

Software engineering and artificial intelligence, obviously. Beyond that:
full-stack web development, developer tools, SaaS products, indie building,
product design and usability, open-source software, and entrepreneurship. I
care about build-in-public practices and about technical writing as a way to
actually learn something rather than skim it.

I am also interested in the relationship between technology and opportunity:
education, access, and the idea that building something useful is a reasonable
way to contribute. I describe that interest as social entrepreneurship, though
I am careful about the word: I do not run a registered social enterprise and I
would rather not imply impact I have not measured.

### Where to go next

The work page has the full professional history, including the parts that are
still in progress. The project archive is the most complete picture of what I
have built. And writing is where I write down the things I learn along the way.

If any of that is interesting, or if you are working on something in a similar
direction, get in touch and we can talk.

## SERVICES PAGE

### What I can build for you

AI products, full-stack apps, SaaS, business systems, websites. Every engagement
ends with something deployed and usable, not a prototype.

### AI Product Development

I build AI-powered applications, SaaS products and intelligent workflows from
concept to deployment. Whether you need a standalone AI product or AI features
integrated into an existing system, I handle the full development lifecycle:
data pipeline design, frontend interfaces and API architecture.

**Who it is for:** Founders building AI products, SaaS companies adding AI
features, businesses looking to automate with AI.
**What to expect:** A production-ready AI application built with modern
frameworks, designed for real users and real data.

### Full-Stack Web Development

Complete web applications built with modern frameworks, from frontend interfaces
to backend APIs, databases, authentication and deployment. Every application is
production-ready, tested and built with scalability in mind.

**Who it is for:** Businesses needing custom web applications, startups building
their first product, teams needing internal tools.
**What to expect:** A complete application with frontend, backend, database,
authentication and deployment, ready for users.

### SaaS Development

End-to-end SaaS product development, from initial concept and MVP to a
production-ready application with authentication, billing, dashboards and
analytics. Built with modern, scalable architectures that grow with your
product.

**Who it is for:** SaaS founders, startups with a product idea, businesses
transitioning to subscription models.
**What to expect:** A complete SaaS product with the core features needed to
launch and start acquiring users.

### AI Integration

Enhance existing products with practical AI capabilities, from LLM-powered
content generation to intelligent data processing and automated workflows. I
focus on AI features that deliver genuine value, not just novelty.

**Who it is for:** Existing products that could benefit from AI, businesses
with data processing needs, teams wanting to automate workflows.
**What to expect:** Practical AI features that improve your product and save
your users time.

### Business Systems

When off-the-shelf software doesn't fit, I build custom business systems:
CRM-style tools, booking platforms, internal dashboards and workflow
applications tailored to your exact requirements.

**Who it is for:** Businesses with unique workflows, clinics needing patient
management, teams needing internal tools.
**What to expect:** A custom-built system designed around your actual workflow,
not forced into a generic template.

### Modern Website Development

Professional, responsive websites built for conversion. Whether you need a
corporate site, a local business presence or a brand showcase, every site is
fast, mobile-first and designed to turn visitors into customers.

**Who it is for:** Businesses, startups, local brands, companies needing a
professional web presence.
**What to expect:** A fast, responsive, conversion-focused website that
represents your brand professionally.

### Website Redesign

Modernize outdated websites with better UX, responsive design, performance and
modern frameworks. I keep what works, rebuild what doesn't and ensure the result
is faster, more professional and easier to maintain.

**Who it is for:** Businesses with outdated websites, companies that have
outgrown their current design, brands needing a refresh.
**What to expect:** A modern, responsive redesign that improves user experience
and performance while maintaining your brand.

### Landing Pages

High-quality landing pages for products, startups, campaigns and businesses.
Focused on conversion, with clear messaging, strong CTAs and responsive design
that works on every device.

**Who it is for:** Product launches, marketing campaigns, startup MVPs, service
promotion.
**What to expect:** A focused, high-converting landing page built and deployed
quickly.

### FAQ

**What services do you offer as a full-stack developer?**
AI product development, full-stack web applications, SaaS product development,
AI integration into existing products, custom business systems, modern website
development, website redesigns and landing pages.

**How do you start a project?**
A short call or email thread to scope the problem, followed by a clear plan:
what gets built, what it costs and when it ships. Work starts once the scope is
agreed.

**Do you work with startups and businesses?**
Yes. Startups building a first product, SaaS companies adding AI features, and

**Where are you based and do you work remotely?**
I am based in Karachi, Pakistan and work remotely with clients anywhere.
Communication happens over email, call or the tool your team already uses.

## PROJECT DETAILS

### TeleCloud

**Category:** Product · Also known as: TeleCloud
**Status:** In Development
**Started:** 2026
**Role:** Creator, Full-Stack Developer

A personal cloud drive that keeps the file bytes inside your own private Telegram
channel.

**Technologies:** Telegram Bot API, Cloud Storage, Web App

**Problem:** Cloud storage usually means trusting a third party with your file
bytes. For sensitive or private files, that is the point of friction.

**Goals:**
- Keep file bytes inside a user's own Telegram channel
- Provide a familiar cloud drive interface
- Minimize third-party data exposure

**My contribution:** Designed and building the full product: the Telegram bot
integration, the web interface, and the storage layer that keeps everything
inside the user's own space.

**Implementation:** Using Telegram's bot API as the storage and sync layer,
with a custom web app on top for the drive experience.

**Challenges:**
- Telegram's file handling limits and how they interact with a cloud-drive UX
- Sync conflict resolution when the same file is touched from multiple devices
- Keeping the experience simple enough that it feels like a drive, not a bot

**Results:**
- Working prototype with file upload, list, and download through Telegram
- Web interface that mirrors the drive metaphor

**Lessons:**
- The hardest part is not the storage, it is the mental model: users expect a
  drive, and a bot API does not naturally provide one.
- Sync semantics matter more than storage semantics for this kind of product.

---

### Formivo

**Category:** Developer Tool · Also known as: Formivo
**Status:** In Development
**Started:** 2026
**Role:** Creator, Full-Stack Developer

A developer-first form endpoint that turns submissions on existing websites into
a lead dashboard.

**Technologies:** API, Dashboard, Web App

**Problem:** Adding a form to an existing site usually means wiring up a backend
endpoint, an inbox, and some kind of lead tracking — or accepting a third-party
form service that owns the data.

**Goals:**
- Give developers a drop-in form endpoint that already has a dashboard
- Turn raw form submissions into scoped, filterable leads
- Keep the access-control model simple enough that a single developer can trust
  it with real submissions

**My contribution:** Built the form endpoint, the lead-ingest pipeline, and the
dashboard. The access-control decision — scoping leads by form, with clear
ownership — shaped the backend more than anything else.

**Implementation:**
- Form endpoint that accepts POST submissions and validates them
- Lead model that scopes submissions by form and adds metadata
- Dashboard that lets the form owner view, filter, and export leads
- Access control that makes sure a submission only appears to the right owner

**Challenges:**
- Deciding what "owned by" means for a form that might be embedded on many sites
- Keeping the inbox useful without becoming a full CRM
- Handling spam and low-quality submissions without making every form owner
  configure anti-spam

**Results:**
- Working form endpoint with a real dashboard
- Lead-scoping model that keeps submissions isolated by form

**Lessons:**
- The access-control decision is not a detail, it is the product. Get it wrong
  and the dashboard is useless because trust is broken.
- A form endpoint is not interesting on its own; the dashboard is what makes it
  worth using.

---

### PasteLink Pro

**Category:** Product · Also known as: PasteLink Pro
**Status:** Maintained
**Started:** 2026
**Role:** Creator, Full-Stack Developer

A no-account text sharing tool with expiry, optional password protection and
burn-after-read.

**Technologies:** Web App, Cryptography, Storage

**Problem:** Quickly sharing a snippet of text or a small file usually means
pasting it into some service and hoping the link is not archived, indexed, or
left live longer than intended.

**Goals:**
- Make sharing a snippet as fast as possible
- Add expiry and optional password protection so the creator has control
- Support burn-after-read so a link disappears after the first open
- Keep the product usable without an account

**My contribution:** Built the full product: the paste creation flow, the
storage and expiry model, the password protection path, and the burn-after-read
semantics.

**Implementation:**
- Paste creation with optional expiry, password, and burn-after-read flags
- Password hashing done client-side, so the server never sees the plaintext
  password (see the write-up on what that actually buys you)
- Expiry as a background process, not a per-request check that blocks reads
- Burn-after-read as a state transition that happens on the first successful
  read

**Challenges:**
- Choosing what client-side password hashing actually protects, and being honest
  about what it does not
- Making burn-after-read feel reliable without making it impossible to recover
  from a bad click
- Keeping the no-account experience fast while still storing enough metadata to
  make expiry and stats useful

**Results:**
- Working product with expiry, password protection, and burn-after-read
- Client-side password hashing for paste access
- Maintained and used

**Lessons:**
- Client-side password hashing is useful, but it is not a substitute for
  transport security or server-side access control.
- Burn-after-read is a feature people ask for more than you expect, and the
  implementation has to be forgiving of real-world use.

---

### Slik

**Category:** Developer Tool · Also known as: Slik
**Status:** In Development
**Started:** 2026
**Role:** Creator, Full-Stack Developer

A CLI that scaffolds a full-stack SaaS starter with authentication, a dashboard
and an admin panel.

**Technologies:** CLI, SaaS Starter, Web App

**Problem:** Starting a SaaS from scratch means making a lot of the same
decisions every time: auth, dashboard layout, admin panel, billing hooks, and
the boring glue around them.

**Goals:**
- Scaffold a usable full-stack SaaS starter in one command
- Include authentication, a dashboard, and an admin panel by default
- Make the starter something a developer can build on rather than something they
  have to undo

**My contribution:** Designed the scaffold template and the CLI that generates
it, with a focus on what a real SaaS needs on day one rather than a demo.

**Implementation:**
- CLI that generates a full-stack project with auth, a dashboard, and an admin
  panel
- Template choices that reflect a real SaaS baseline rather than a toy app
- Room to add billing, email, and other SaaS-adjacent pieces as needed

**Challenges:**
- Picking defaults that are useful without being opinionated enough to get in
  the way
- Keeping the generated project readable and editable, not a black box
- Balancing completeness with simplicity: too much included and it feels heavy,
  too little and it is not useful

**Results:**
- Working CLI with a real SaaS starter template
- Auth, dashboard, and admin panel included

**Lessons:**
- The best scaffold is the one someone actually extends. That means readable
  generated code and a clear seam between the starter and the custom work.
- A SaaS starter is not a SaaS. It is the part of the SaaS that is the same
  every time.

---

### PromptAudit

**Category:** AI Tool · Also known as: PromptAudit
**Status:** Prototype
**Started:** 2026
**Role:** Creator, AI Product Builder

An AI tool that audits a website for SEO, GEO and AEO and generates the fix
prompts for it.

**Technologies:** AI, LLM, Web App, SEO, GEO, AEO

**Problem:** Websites can be technically sound and still be invisible to answer
engines, generative search, and AI assistants that summarize rather than link.
Traditional SEO tooling does not cover that gap well.

**Goals:**
- Audit a website for SEO, GEO, and AEO in one place
- Produce fixes that are specific enough to act on
- Generate the prompts that would guide an AI assistant or a developer toward
  those fixes

**My contribution:** Designed the audit model and the prompt-generation path.
This is a prototype, so the emphasis is on whether the idea is worth pursuing
rather than on polishing a finished product.

**Implementation:**
- Audit that looks at SEO basics, GEO readiness, and AEO suitability
- Output that includes both a human-readable summary and prompts that can be fed
  back into an AI assistant for remediation
- Focused on actionable output rather than a generic score

**Challenges:**
- Defining GEO and AEO in a way that is testable, not just marketing language
- Making the prompts useful rather than generic
- Not overpromising on what an audit can say before the site is actually
  crawled and understood

**Results:**
- Prototype that audits and produces fix prompts
- A working model for how SEO, GEO, and AEO can be evaluated together

**Lessons:**
- GEO and AEO are not the same as SEO, and treating them as synonyms produces
  weak audits.
- Prompt generation is only useful if the prompts are specific enough to act on.
